SUC2.name: Invertase
SUC2.role: Cleaves sucrose into glucose and fructose — the classic yeast sugar story.
SUC2.phenotype: Lets yeast break table sugar into fuel it can burn.

steps.label: SUC2 locus
steps.plain_english: On chromosome IX sits a stretch of DNA that encodes invertase. This is the recipe — not the enzyme yet.

steps.label: SUC2 transcript
steps.plain_english: The cell copies that DNA into messenger RNA — a working draft the ribosome can read. DNA stays in the nucleus; mRNA carries the message out.

steps.label: Invertase enzyme
steps.plain_english: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into invertase. The finished enzyme cleaves sucrose → glucose + fructose — fuel yeast can actually use.

ACT1.name: Actin
ACT1.role: Builds the cytoskeleton — the cell's internal scaffolding. Highly conserved across fungi.
ACT1.phenotype: Same job in every fungus: shape, movement, and division scaffolding.

steps.label: ACT1 locus
steps.plain_english: Actin is one of the most conserved genes in eukaryotes. The DNA sequence is almost a family signature across fungi.

steps.label: actin mRNA
steps.plain_english: Transcribed constantly — cells need a steady supply of actin monomers to rebuild filaments as they grow and divide.

steps.label: actin monomer
steps.plain_english: Monomers polymerize into filaments that push, pull, and hold the cell together. Change the sequence a little and the scaffold still works — change it a lot and the cell collapses.

bakers-yeast.label: S. cerevisiae ACT1
bakers-yeast.note: Budding yeast actin — classic lab reference.

schizosaccharomyces.label: S. pombe act1
schizosaccharomyces.note: Fission yeast — same protein job, slightly different sequence handwriting.

neurospora.label: N. crassa act
neurospora.note: Filamentous mold — conserved core, divergent tips.

HO.name: Homothallic endonuclease
HO.role: Cuts mating-type DNA so yeast can switch mating type — a yeast-specific story.
HO.phenotype: Enables mating-type switching; not found the same way in fission yeast or molds.

steps.label: HO endonuclease gene
steps.plain_english: HO encodes a site-specific DNA cutter. Only budding yeast tells this particular mating-type switch story.

steps.label: HO transcript
steps.plain_english: Expressed in a tight window of the cell cycle — timing matters as much as the sequence.

steps.label: HO endonuclease
steps.plain_english: The enzyme nicks mating-type DNA, triggering gene conversion. Result: a cell can change which mating partner it seeks.

TEF1.name: Translation elongation factor 1-α
TEF1.role: Helps ribosomes add amino acids during protein building. Conserved across fungi (also called EF1A).
TEF1.phenotype: Without it, protein synthesis stalls — every cell needs this machinery.

steps.label: TEF1 / EF1A locus
steps.plain_english: A housekeeping gene for translation. Yeast keeps redundant copies because the cell cannot afford to run out.

steps.label: TEF1 mRNA
steps.plain_english: Abundant transcript — translation factors are among the most expressed messages in a growing cell.

steps.label: eEF1A
steps.plain_english: Shuttles aminoacyl-tRNAs into the ribosome. Same core job from yeast to humans — evolutionary handwriting with a shared ink.

EF1A.name: Elongation factor 1-α
EF1A.role: Alias family for TEF1 — translation machinery; highly conserved.
EF1A.phenotype: Same translation job under a different name in some annotations.

steps.label: EF1A locus
steps.plain_english: Annotation alias for the elongation-factor family. See TEF1 for the baker's-yeast story.

steps.label: EF1A mRNA
steps.plain_english: The message that keeps protein synthesis moving.

steps.label: EF-1α
steps.plain_english: The finished elongation factor — shared core across fungi.
